name: Step-up
equipment: a step or sturdy box, 15–20 cm, or a stair
movement: a step up onto a box with one leg, standing tall, and a controlled step down

phone.placement: Stand the phone up on the floor, leaning on something, two or three metres away, side on to where you will be.

words.hint: Side on to a step: one foot on it, drive up to standing tall, lower with control.
words.start: Stand the phone up on the floor. Stand side on to it with the foot nearest the phone flat on the step.
words.position: Stand tall, side on to the phone, with the whole of the foot nearest the phone flat on the step and the other foot on the floor.
words.top: Standing tall on the step on one leg — knee and hip straight, chest up — the other foot lightly beside it.
howto: Start on the bottom stair or a step 10–20 cm high, with a rail or wall to hold if you need it. Go higher as it gets easy, no higher than mid-shin.
Stand side on to the phone with the foot nearest it flat on the step, the whole foot on it. Chest up.
Push through that foot and stand up tall on the step — knee and hip fully straight — bringing the other foot up to tap the step. The back foot only follows; no push from it.
Lower the back foot to the floor slowly, over two seconds. The rep counts there. Do a set on one leg, then the other.
words.cannot: The knee caving inward and the pelvis dropping: it judges the stepping leg from the side — its knee and hip at the top, its shin at the start — and the trunk. Keep the knee over the second toe yourself.
words.about: Step-up — standing side on with one foot on a step: the stepping knee, at least 165° at the top, and the hip, as the angle between shoulder and knee, at least 160°, so you stand fully tall rather than stay bent; the trunk within 15° of vertical at the top and no more than 30° forward on the way up; and the shin, as the knee's lean forward of the ankle, at most 30°. The rep is under way once the knee opens past 155° and counts when it is bent again under 145°; the lowering takes two seconds.
words.lost: Step into the camera, side on
words.safety: Start with a low step and something to hold. Stop if the knee hurts at the front; use a lower step.
words.easier: A lower step; a hand on a rail; a shorter pause at the top.
words.harder: A higher step, no higher than the knee; dumbbells; a slower lowering.
words.mistakes: Pushing off the back foot; throwing the trunk forward at the step; not standing fully tall at the top; the knee collapsing inward; dropping down without control; a step too high.

measurements.label: knee angle

settings.label: Knee angle at the top, at least

measurements.why: The stepping knee: about 105–120 with the foot on a 15–20 cm step, 180 standing tall. Also the progress measurement: under way past 155, back down under 145.

measurements.label: shoulder, hip, knee

settings.label: Hip angle at the top, at least

measurements.why: Standing fully tall opens the hip to 180; staying bent forward at the top leaves it short.

measurements.label: trunk off vertical
measurements.why: The hip-to-shoulder line off plumb, + leaning forward, judged at the top: standing tall on the step.

measurements.label: lean in the push

settings.label: Trunk forward while stepping up, at most (degrees)

measurements.why: The same trunk line, all the way up: some forward lean is natural as the weight comes over the step; past 30 the body is being thrown at it rather than pushed up by the leg.

measurements.label: knee ahead of ankle

settings.label: Knee ahead of the ankle, at most

measurements.why: The shin off vertical: the knee travels forward on a step-up, but well past the toes the step is too high or the foot too far back.

measurements.label: thigh from straight down
measurements.why: 0 standing, 90 thigh level. Not judged: it picks the leg on the step, whose thigh is raised at the start.

faults.label: Knee past the toes
faults.text: Knee back over your foot — whole foot on the step
faults.deep: The step is too high, or the foot too far back — knee over the foot

faults.label: Throwing forward
faults.text: Chest up — push with the leg on the step

faults.label: Leaning forward
faults.deep: Stand up straighter — the trunk is still folded over the step

faults.label: Knee not straight
faults.text: Stand up tall — straighten the knee
faults.deep: All the way up — straighten the knee fully on the step

faults.label: Hips not through
faults.deep: Push the hips through — you are still bent at the top

settings.label: Knee angle that counts as up
